findings.aspect: native accessibility identifiers and action discovery
findings.claim: Most card descendants expose rr.card instead of their required identifiers. The root identifier is repeated on heading, item, options, notes, gate, primary, keep, progress, result and done. Size controls are an observed exception. Required control targets therefore cannot be found by the supplied collector.
reasons: C01 snapshot 0 contains separately named native buttons for Refund to your card, Choose a resolution and Keep my purchase, all identified rr.card; rr.option.cash and rr.primary are absent.

Native reveal diagnostics reach the bottom or bounded step limit without those identifiers. This proves the identifier/discovery defect; it does not prove that a physically tapped, name-selected button would emit an incorrect action.
All six iOS manifests have test exit 65 and native issues, despite the wrapper status captured_not_graded.
findings.repairRecommendation: Make the root a distinct accessibility container without propagating its identifier over descendants; verify unique IDs in the actual native tree before action replay.

findings.claim: SwiftUI disabled styling fades the authored disabled subtree and primary fill/text. Measured flat/core text colors exceed the public RGB tolerance, and disabled reasons are visibly much dimmer than the required secondary text.
reasons: Dark disabled reason text in C02 snapshot 6 and C04 snapshot 5 has dominant core RGB 103,113,112; required secondary is 180,192,187.
C02 snapshot 16 disabled action fill is 39,51,48 versus required 52,68,60, and its text is 113,126,120 versus 186,200,192.

Light C01 snapshot 7 fill is 239,242,240 versus required 223,230,225; text is 164,171,167 versus required 89,101,94. Native frames select the pixel crops; antialias edge colors were not used as the foreground sample.
findings.repairRecommendation: Preserve native disabled semantics while providing a button style whose disabled appearance retains the explicit palette; verify disabled option, size and primary pixels in light and dark.

findings.aspect: runtime base typography of total values
findings.claim: The total-value text uses a 24sp base style instead of the specified 18-unit semibold money/total token (permitted native variation is at most two units).
reasons: The native TextLayoutResult style fields report font_sp 24.0 for Choose an option in C01 and No additional charge in C02; font_weight is 600.

Other strings equal to totalValue can also occur in amount rows, so the scratch set of 15/18/24 values is not treated as a total-only query. The cited unique labels and source call identify the actual summary value.
This is a base-size finding. The resolved font family and final glyph font at enlarged scaling are separate, unassessed aspects.
findings.repairRecommendation: Use the money/total 18sp semibold style for the summary value; retain stronger hierarchy than 15sp amount rows.

findings.aspect: source-declared base typography of total values
findings.claim: The SwiftUI summary passes the 24-point heading metric to totalValue, exceeding the public 18-unit money/total token and its two-unit tolerance. The actual resolved runtime font size is not provided by this collector.
reasons: The finding is limited to the source-declared base style: heading is initialized to 24 and reused by summary totalValue.
Screenshots show the corresponding large emphasis, but pixels and AX frames alone are not used to claim an exact actual resolved native font size.
findings.repairRecommendation: Declare the total using the 18-point money metric and verify actual Dynamic Type separately.

findings.claim: Decorative parcel, chevron and success/checkmark images remain individually present in the native test tree with names such as Box, Go Down and Selected. Whether these nodes are independently traversed by VoiceOver is not established by the exported fields.
reasons: The parcel and success checkmark have native image role 43 and are hittable when visible, despite their decorative intent.

XCUI image presence/hittability does not itself export isAccessibilityElement, hidden traits, or VoiceOver traversal. Thus the actual decorative-hiding violation is suspected, not asserted as a complete native-AX failure.
findings.repairRecommendation: Inspect native accessibility hidden/element traits or a VoiceOver traversal after fixing container semantics.

findings.aspect: observed controlled selection, gate and action behavior
findings.claim: The supplied Android state records show matching effective-option selection and primary enabled state at each examined snapshot. Fifteen actual semantic OnClick callbacks match the supplied action arguments; disabled size/primary/option attempts are blocked without callbacks.
reasons: The comparison uses the actual input model at fixture_index, native selected/enabled fields and gate labels, rather than source declarations. All five gate-precedence messages are represented across the six cases.
C01 selection, C02 size/acknowledgement and C03/C06 notes emit requests while the fixture index remains unchanged; later caller updates change the observed tree.
C05 credit and C06 refund submit traces contain sizeId null and acknowledgementAccepted false, excluding irrelevant caller values.
This collector invokes native semantic OnClick; physical OS touch and a separately executed accessibility service activation are not established.

findings.aspect: actual size action and delayed caller echo
findings.claim: The one successful iOS business activation is rr.size.l: it emits selectSize(l) once while the caller fixture remains initial. The size remains unselected until the caller applies its size-selection update.
reasons: Step 2 callback_delta contains exactly one event with sizeId l and fixture_index 0. Native selected state is false in the pending-size-echo state and true after the caller update.
The same runtime instance and PID are retained. Other iOS controls were not actually activated because their identifiers were unavailable.

findings.claim: The C04 caller replacement removes the old item text and exposes the new Trail desk lamp item in both platforms while retaining each platform’s runtime instance.
reasons: Initial native labels contain Ridge insulated bottle. Replacement snapshots contain Trail desk lamp and no old item-title matches.
Android binding instance remains constant; iOS instance 650EC7E6-660F-49DB-9346-8F0D4C9FFB00 and PID 21664 remain constant.
This checks the item replacement and selected state observed in the tree, not every visible string or every possible caseId replacement.

findings.claim: The examined submitting and complete states show the requested progress/result and total content. iOS progress exposes the caller busy value In progress. The full accessibility/status contract is not established because iOS region identifiers are overridden and Android stateDescription/heading traits are not exported.
reasons: C01/C06 submitting snapshots contain header/item, progress, summary and no editing control tags in Android; sampled images show the corresponding structure.
C05 complete contains result strings and Done; Android Done emits done without changing the fixture. The iOS Done action is unexecuted because rr.done cannot be found.
The iOS native progress aggregate label includes both progress strings and its native value equals In progress.

findings.claim: Android image_bounds_px are incompatible with the actual screenshot extent and must not be used directly for pixel or hit geometry conclusions. Native dp bounds are a separate measurement.
reasons: C03 snapshot 0 image width is 533 pixels, yet the root image_bounds_px right edge is 1465.75.
The bundled collector multiplies raw physical bounds by image.width/(view.width/density), introducing an extra density factor. This is an observation-method error, not a component layout failure.
iOS disabled pixel crops use iOS image_frame, which matches its native 3x screenshot dimensions. No Android image_bounds_px was used to locate product pixels.

findings.aspect: unassessed runtime typography, traits, physical hit geometry and visual completeness
findings.claim: Resolved native font family, exact iOS font sizes, actual VoiceOver hidden/heading traits, physical touch dispatch, and complete clipping/color acceptance remain unassessed. Sampled contact sheets are not full-case visual acceptance.
reasons: Android exports base TextLayoutResult style size/weight/color and environment fontScale, but no resolved font-family identity. iOS exports native Dynamic Type category and AX bounds, not resolved glyph font properties.

158 fully visible Android native touchBoundsInRoot measurements meet the corresponding reported minimum targets; this does not prove physical OS touch dispatch or iOS touch rectangles. iOS frames are AX geometry.

Only eight sampled screenshots per case/platform were visually inspected via contact sheets. All supplied snapshot metadata/trees/actions were processed, but every image and every overlap interval was not examined.

Updated long-content states, notably Android C03 expanded notes, are not supplied as an independently complete overlapping sweep: the baseline sweep request becomes a single capture. Offscreen text presence does not establish visible unclipped glyphs.
Current minimum-OS runtime and package compatibility were not recompiled or executed in this read-only phase.

findings.claim: At accessibility5 the three roughly 100.7-point size columns fragment ordinary labels such as Large and Medium across short lines. All-character visibility may still be satisfied; the stronger readability concern is suspected rather than a confirmed clipping failure.
reasons: The sampled native image shows Lar/ge and Me/diu/... while native size frames retain three columns across 326 content points.

The contract permits natural growth and wrapping. No missing glyph or overlap was established from these samples; this is a recommendation to improve enlarged-text flow, not an asserted hidden failure.
findings.repairRecommendation: Allow size-choice columns/flow width to grow with Dynamic Type so ordinary words can move to fewer columns.

coverageSummary.nativeRecordsScope: All supplied C01-C06 observation JSON snapshots, model fixture indices and action-step/callback records were processed on both platforms. Per-snapshot derived records are preserved in inventory.json, typed-checks.json and semantic-state-checks.json.
coverageSummary.visualSampling: Eight source PNG frames sampled for each of six cases on each platform (96 total), viewed in twelve labelled contact sheets. This is an honest sampled scan, not a whole-card clipping pass. Pixel crops are derived from native iOS frames for three disabled contexts.
coverageSummary.businessScope: All five gate-precedence conditions represented; native selected/enabled states compared to caller effective choices. Android 15 callbacks examined; iOS one actual size callback examined and remaining requested business activations mostly unavailable from ID loss.
coverageSummary.geometryScope: 158 fully visible Android reported native touch rectangles checked against minima with no observed violations. iOS AX frames examined for target identity/position only. No physical hit-test inference.
coverageSummary.typographyScope: Android native base style total-size finding and Swift source base-style finding; native font families and exact resolved iOS font sizes remain unassessed.
coverageSummary.colorScope: Disabled palette pixel samples confirm iOS alpha/color failure. Other roles were visually sampled but not all quantitatively assigned and verified.
